objective.text: Use counters to make equal groups. Equal groups have the same number in each group.

explanations.title: Equal groups have the same number
explanations.text: Groups are equal when each group has the same number of counters. 3 groups with 2 counters in each are equal. A group of 4 and a group of 2 are unequal.

explanations.title: Say how many groups
explanations.text: To tell about equal groups, say: There are 4 groups of 2 counters. The first number is how many groups. The second number is how many in each group.

explanations.title: Many ways to make equal groups
explanations.text: You can make equal groups in more than one way. 12 counters make 2 groups of 6. They also make 3 groups of 4, 4 groups of 3, or 6 groups of 2.

explanations.title: Make unequal groups equal
explanations.text: Look at the group with the most counters and the group with the fewest. Move one counter from the most to the fewest. Keep checking until every group has the same number.

explanations.title: Split into 2 equal groups
explanations.text: To make 2 equal groups, share the counters into two rows. Or split them in half. A doubles fact can help you check.

examples.text: 6 counters in 3 groups of 2 are equal. Every group has 2. Move them to 4 in one group and 2 in another. Now the groups are unequal.

examples.title: 8 counters
examples.text: 8 counters in groups of 2 make 4 groups. The same 8 counters in groups of 4 make 2 groups.

examples.title: 12 counters in equal groups
examples.text: 12 counters can make 2 groups of 6. They can make 3 groups of 4. They can make 4 groups of 3. They can make 6 groups of 2.

examples.title: 10 counters

examples.title: Make 3, 5 and 4 equal
examples.text: Three groups have 3, 5 and 4 counters. Move 1 counter from the group of 5 to the group of 3. Now there are 3 groups of 4.

explanations.title: Add the groups
explanations.text: 4 groups have 3 counters each. To find the total, add the number in each group. 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3 equals 12. This is repeated addition.

explanations.title: Draw groups of circles
explanations.text: In math, we draw circles to show groups. Draw a big circle for each group. Draw the same number of small circles in each. Draw a line under each group.

explanations.title: The repeating number
explanations.text: The number that repeats is how many are in each group. The number of times it repeats is how many groups there are. 4 groups of 3 gives 3 plus 3 plus 3 plus 3.

objective.text: Use drawings of equal groups and repeated addition. Use doubles to add faster.

explanations.title: Add one group at a time
explanations.text: 4 groups of 4 is 4 plus 4 plus 4 plus 4. Add one group at a time. 4 plus 4 is 8. 8 plus 4 is 12. 12 plus 4 is 16.

explanations.title: Use doubles to bundle groups
explanations.text: Pair the groups. 4 plus 4 is 8. Then there is another 4 plus 4, which is 8. 8 plus 8 is 16. So 4 groups of 4 is the same as 2 groups of 8.

explanations.title: Skip-count to add
explanations.text: You can skip-count to add equal groups. For 4 groups of 5, count 5, 10, 15, 20. The total is 20.

explanations.title: Same total, new groups
explanations.text: 4 groups of 5 and 2 groups of 10 have the same total, 20. You only group the circles in a new way. Each group of 10 has 2 fives.

source_ref.section: Concept Development (4 groups of 5 and 2 groups of 10)

explanations.title: Pair the addends, then add on the extra
explanations.text: Group the addends in pairs and use doubles. If one addend is left over, add it on at the end. 5 twos is 4 plus 4 plus 2, which is 10.

examples.title: 4 groups of 4

objective.text: Draw a tape diagram to show equal groups. Write repeated addition to find the total.

explanations.title: Parts and whole in a tape diagram
explanations.text: A tape diagram has boxes. Each box is a part. When you know the parts, you add them to find the whole. 2 plus 3 plus 1 equals 6.

explanations.title: Boxes are groups
explanations.text: Each box is one group. The number inside the box is how many are in that group. 3 boxes with 2 in each box is 3 groups of 2.

explanations.title: Add the same unit again
explanations.text: With equal groups you add the same number again and again. 2 plus 2 plus 2 equals 6. We are adding twos. We can add units of 2, 5 or any number.

explanations.title: Make the boxes equal
explanations.text: Boxes can start with different numbers, like 2, 3, 5 and 2. Move counters so every box has 3. Now there are 4 equal groups of 3.

explanations.title: Swap the groups and the number in each
explanations.text: 4 groups of 3 and 3 groups of 4 both equal 12. For 3 groups of 4, draw 3 boxes and write 4 in each box.

objective.text: Solve word problems involving addition of equal groups in rows and columns.

explanations.title: Rows and columns as groups
explanations.text: In an array, each row is a group. Each column is also a group. Count the equal groups, then add them.

explanations.title: Parts of a tape diagram

explanations.title: Answer in a sentence
explanations.text: After you find the total, write a statement. Say what the total counts. For example, there are 20 desks in the room.

objective.text: Use rectangular arrays to investigate odd and even numbers.

explanations.title: Even plus even
explanations.text: Join two even arrays. The total is even. 6 plus 8 equals 14. 14 is even.

explanations.title: Even plus odd
explanations.text: An odd number has one tile sticking out. Join an even and an odd and one tile still sticks out. The total is odd.

explanations.title: Odd plus odd
explanations.text: Two odd numbers each have one tile sticking out. The two extra tiles make a pair. The total is even.

explanations.title: It works for bigger numbers
explanations.text: The same rules work for larger numbers. 10 plus 12 equals 22. Both addends are even and the total is even.

explanations.title: Skip-count by twos
explanations.text: Count by ones and knock on the twos. Then say only the twos: 2, 4, 6, 8 and on to 20.
